stories.title: Numerical simulation of dynamic mechanical responses of rock with a pre-existing hole under different loading directions
stories.description: The instability of roadway cross-section surrounding rock caused by impact disturbance is closely related to stress redistribution, crack propagation, and energy dissipation around the roadway cross-section. To clarify the influence of impact velocity and loading direction on the failure mechanism of rock with a D-shaped hole, a split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) numerical model of granite with a D-shaped hole was established using HyperMesh. The Riedel–Hiermaier–Thoma (RHT) material model was selected to describe the dynamic damage and fragmentation response of the rock. Impact velocities of 6, 8, and 10 m/s were used in the numerical simulations, with the loading direction forming angles of 0°, 45°, 90°, 135°, and 180° to the axis of the D-shaped hole. The stress evolution, damage development, fragmentation characteristics, and energy evolution mechanisms were systematically analyzed. The results show that the increase in impact velocity intensifies the stress concentration around the hole and advances the formation of high-stress zones. The damage initially occurs at the arch foot of the D-shaped hole or at other geometric discontinuities, and then extends toward both ends of the sample, resulting in an X-shaped failure mode. As the impact velocity increases, the damaged volume expands, but the promoting effect gradually weakens at higher velocities. The loading direction significantly influences the spatial distribution of the stress concentration zones and the final failure mode. Oblique loading (especially at 135°) produces the largest damaged volume and the most severe fragmentation, while the loading directions of 0° and 180° lead to relatively larger fragments. The fragment size distribution can be well described by both the Weibull distribution and the three-parameter GEV function, with the Weibull distribution exhibiting higher fitting accuracy. Energy analysis indicates that the internal energy is mainly consumed in the initiation and propagation of cracks, while the kinetic energy is associated with the motion of fragments. Under oblique loading, more incident energy is converted into internal energy related to fracture, thereby forming a more developed crack network. These findings help clarify the dynamic failure mechanism of roadway cross-section surrounding rock and provide a theoretical basis for support design under impact disturbance.

stories.title: Catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation for precise synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes
stories.description: Organic semiconductors such as polythiophenes (PThs) offer substantial potential for flexible optoelectronics. Incorporating silicon into the PTh backbone represents a promising strategy to enhance flexibility and tune electronic properties; however, conventional metal-catalyzed synthetic approaches lack precise control over polymer chain growth, yielding materials with poorly defined energy levels and relatively board dispersity. Here, we report a catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation (TDP) strategy for the direct incorporation of silicon into PThs, producing a class of narrowly dispersed silicon-incorporated polymers. This thermally driven, radical-mediated mechanism circumvents the uncontrolled initiation and competitive pathways of conventional catalytic routes, enabling precise control over chain growth and yielding well-defined PThs with narrow dispersity (Đ = 1.2 – 1.4). The dehydrogenatively coupled diphenylsilane- terthiophene polymer (PS-1) shows favorable energy-level alignment and a hole mobility of 9.2 × 10−4 cm2 V−1 s−1. When employed as a hole-transport interlayer in inverted tin-lead (Sn-Pb) perovskite solar cells, PS-1 enables a champion power conversion efficiency of 23.3% with enhanced operational stability, surpassing the 20.8% efficiency of standard PEDOT:PSS-based devices. This work establishes a scalable synthetic route to advanced conjugated polymers, providing a versatile materials platform for optoelectronic applications. The synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes typically requires metal catalysts, which show poor polymerisation control and require post-synthesis purification. Here, the authors report a metal catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation strategy for the synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes with well defined structures, narrow dispersities and high charge carrier mobilities.

stories.title: A macrocyclic peptide inhibitor of the antibiotic transporter NorA
stories.description: Staphylococcus aureus is a human bacterial pathogen with an array of molecular mechanisms to evade the action of antibiotics. Within the organism, efflux pumps provide a first-line defense mechanism, enabling broad multidrug resistance across antibiotic classes and the ability for the organism to evolve target-level resistance mechanisms. NorA is a key efflux transporter in S. aureus responsible for conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones, puromycin, and other cytotoxic compounds. Here, we describe an approach to develop peptide efflux pump inhibitors (EPIs) of NorA by leveraging chemical synthesis and design, structure-based insights, and screening approaches to probe NorA pocket engagement and S. aureus growth inhibition. Our cryo-EM structure reveals that a lead peptide NPI-5 inserts deeply into NorA’s substrate binding pocket by using two tryptophan-arginine motifs to bind an anionic patch within NorA, thereby stabilizing the outward-facing conformation of the transporter and halting antibiotic efflux. Further optimization of NPI-5 involving unnatural residues and macrocyclization yielded cNPI-7, a peptide which potentiates fluoroquinolones in vitro and in a murine bacteremia infection model. The successful development of potent and selective peptide-based EPIs provides an approach for inhibiting other efflux systems from pathogenic organisms. In this work, peptide efflux pump inhibitors were developed for Staphylococcus aureus NorA to serve as antibiotic adjuvants by leveraging chemical synthesis and design, structure-based insights, and screening approaches to probe NorA pocket engagement.

stories.title: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
stories.description: Aortic aneurysm and dissection (AAD) are life-threatening cardiovascular diseases with limited therapeutic options. It is essential to identify new risk factors and therapeutic targets for AAD. Recent evidence has highlighted the role of gut microbiota in AAD, yet the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identify phenylacetylglutamine (PAGln), a gut microbiota–derived metabolite, is associated with increased risk for AAD. Our study illustrates that elevated plasma PAGln levels were independently associated with increased AAD risk in a clinical cohort comprising 1,144 individuals. Exogenous PAGln supplementation exacerbated AAD in male mice, whereas AAV8-mediated hepatic knockdown of Glyat reduced circulating metabolite levels and ameliorated AAD. We further demonstrated that the elevated PAGln levels observed in disease are gut microbiota–dependent in origin. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that PAGln exacerbates AAD by expanding a pro-inflammatory IL6 (high) macrophage subpopulation. Mechanistically, PAGln directly binds to integrin α5β1 and downregulates the repressive H3K27me3 levels via the integrin α5β1–integrin-linked kinase (ILK)–lysine demethylase 6B (KDM6B) signaling, thereby enhancing IL6 transcriptional permissiveness. Genetic ablation of integrin β1, the receptor for PAGln, effectively ameliorated AAD in male mice. Our findings identify PAGln is associated with increased risk for AAD and reveal its potential as a therapeutic target. Here the authors report a link between the gut microbial metabolite PAGln and aortic aneurysm and dissection in patients and show that it worsens disease in mice by promoting inflammation in the aortic wall.

stories.title: Highly reinforced self-cleaning low-density polyethylene/poly(vinyl butyral)/bismuth oxide nanocomposites fabricated by electron beam irradiation
stories.description: In this work, highly reinforced self-cleaning nanocomposites based on low-density polyethylene (LDPE), polyvinyl butyral (PVB), and bismuth oxide (Bi2O3) nanoparticles were successfully fabricated using electron-beam (EB) irradiation. LDPE/PVB blends with varying PVB contents were prepared to improve matrix compatibility. Among the investigated compositions, the LDPE/PVB (95/5 wt%) blend exhibited the optimum properties and was subsequently reinforced with 3 parts per hundred resin (phr) Bi2O3 nanoparticles to fabricate LDPE/PVB/Bi2O3 nanocomposites. The LDPE/PVB (95/5 wt%) composition showed optimum performance. Reinforcement with 3 parts per hundred resin (phr) Bi2O3 nanoparticles to fabricate LDPE/PVB/Bi2O3 nanocomposites using a Brabender-like mixing apparatus and subsequent exposure to EB irradiation at different doses (10–150 kGy). Gel fraction and crosslink density calculations confirmed that EB irradiation up to 100 kGy provides the optimum dose, as radiation-induced crosslinking strengthens the polymer network and results in pronounced improvements in mechanical strength, thermal stability, and interfacial interaction. Comprehensive characterizations were performed using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscopy (TEM), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and contact angle measurements. The results confirmed homogeneous Bi2O3 nanoparticle dispersion, enhanced structural integrity, and improved surface properties. The synergistic effect of PVB/Bi2O3 incorporation into LDPE and EB irradiation markedly increased hydrophobicity, raising the water contact angle from 93° (neat LDPE) to 142° (irradiated nanocomposite). Furthermore, photocatalytic self-cleaning efficiency was significantly enhanced, achieving 94% methylene blue degradation under UV irradiation, compared to only 16% for neat LDPE. The kinetic analysis confirmed that the pseudo-first-order model provided superior correlation (R² = 0.985–0.998), establishing photocatalysis as the dominant degradation pathway. Overall, the developed LDPE/PVB/Bi2O3 nanocomposites exhibited superior mechanical strength, thermal stability, hydrophobicity, and self-cleaning performance, demonstrating their potential for advanced packaging, environmental remediation, and outdoor engineering applications requiring durable multifunctional polymeric materials.

stories.title: AI-assisted chest CT scan analysis of body composition at ICU admission and 6-month mortality
stories.description: Abnormal body composition at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with worse survival, but it is rarely measured in practice because manual CT analysis is labor-intensive. We conducted a secondary analysis of a single-center prospective cohort of 509 patients who underwent chest CT within 24 h of ICU admission, of whom 475 were included in the final analysis. Open-source AI segmentation was used to quantify body composition, and the resulting features were related to 6-month survival. Risk scores derived from body composition were significantly associated with 6-month survival (p < 0.001, log-rank test). In five-fold cross-validation, the AUC for discriminating survivors from non-survivors was 0.73; when feature selection was accounted for, the AUC was 0.68 by nested cross-validation and 0.69 by bootstrap optimism correction. The study shows that the automated AI-based analysis of admission chest CT yields body composition scores significantly associated with 6-month mortality after ICU admission.
